NAPA, California, Nov 4 : OpenAI President Greg Brockman said on Wednesday the company now generates the majority of its revenue from enterprise sales and he believes it will be ready to go public in 2027. Brockman said the AI lab has been ramping up sales to businesses in competition with rival Anthropic, which is likely to go public before year end, including pushing its Codex agent. The AI executive spoke at a Wall Street Journal tech conference in Napa, California. When asked on stage if OpenAI will be ready for an IPO next year, he said, "I think so."  San Francisco's OpenAI has been racing to ramp up fundraising, Reuters reported, in order to capitalize on its recent growth after delaying its IPO plans.

Source: Reuters

TOKYO, Nov 5 : The dollar edged lower on Thursday in the aftermath of an overwhelming victory by Democrats in US midterm elections that cleared a major source of uncertainty and fuelled a rally in global equities. The yen firmed after minutes of the Bank of Japan's September meeting reinforced expectations for further interest rate hikes, while sterling held near a seven-week high ahead of a Bank of England policy decision expected to deliver another rate increase. Democrats swept to sizable majorities in the Senate and House of Representatives, easing concerns about contested results and spurring gains in US Treasuries and equities around the world. The election result raises prospects of political gridlock in Washington and lowers expectations that US President Donald Trump will resume military strikes against Iran, said Ray Attrill, head of FX strategy at National Australia Bank. "A lot of the market moves that we're seeing, particularly in bonds, I think can be traced directly to that, as well as a weaker dollar on the back of lower Treasury yields," Attrill said on a podcast.

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, fell 0.06 per cent to 101.41, after a 0.36 per cent decline in the prior session. The euro was up 0.12 per cent at $1.1241. The yen strengthened 0.08 per cent to 158.25 per dollar. Despite the political shift in the US, expectations for the Federal Reserve's interest rate path remained largely intact. Markets are pricing in an 81.2 per cent chance for a rate increase of at least 25 basis points from the Fed at its December meeting, according to CME FedWatch, up from 77.4 per cent in the prior session.  The ADP National Employment Report showed US private payrolls rose by 86,000 jobs in October, above the 69,000 estimate of economists polled by Reuters. The report was the latest in a string of labor market data this week, which will wind up on Friday with the release of the government's payrolls report. Sterling was up 0.38 per cent at $1.3462, after rising to a more than seven-week high of $1.3503 ahead of the Bank of England's policy announcement on Thursday. The pound was poised for its sixth straight daily gain, its longest run higher since an eight-session streak that ended on July 6.  The BOE expected to raise rates to contend with inflation pressure from soaring energy costs, although it may push back against investors' bets that several more increases will follow next year. The Bank of Japan meeting minutes from September, when policymakers raised rates to a 31-year high of 1.25 per cent, underscored expectations for further tightening, with one board member signalling scope for faster increases. The Australian dollar strengthened 0.09 per cent versus the greenback to $0.701, while New Zealand's kiwi climbed 0.12 per cent to $0.5627.   In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin gained 0.60 per cent to $80,660.59, and ether rose 0.45 per cent to $2,428.15.

Source: Reuters

TOKYO, Nov 5 : Japan's service sector expanded modestly in October as activity and new orders both rose slightly faster, a business survey showed on Thursday. • The S&P Global final Japan Services Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) edged higher to 51.7 in October from 51.3 in September, a survey by S&P Global showed, marking a fifth straight month of expansion but coming in below the flash reading of 52.0. The 50-mark separates growth from contraction • New orders increased for a 28th straight month, with the pace of growth picking up from September, as firms cited firmer domestic demand, new clients and business development efforts as factors • In contrast, foreign demand remained weak, though the decline in new export orders eased to its slowest since April

• Cost pressures eased further, with input price inflation decelerating for a fourth straight month to an eight-month low. Output price inflation also moderated, although charges have now risen every month for the past four and a half years • Business confidence weakened to its lowest level since March, as concerns over inflation, an ageing population and labour shortages tempered optimism about growth in the defence and technology sectors, business expansion plans and increased tourism • Persistent inflation "could also constrain demand and hiring in the months ahead," said Annabel Fiddes, economics associate director at S&P Global Market Intelligence • "Whether growth loses further momentum and cost pressures ease will be important considerations for the Bank of Japan as it assesses further policy tightening," Fiddes added • Employment rose only marginally, marking the weakest pace of job creation in the current 14-month hiring stretch, the survey showed. Companies cited expansion plans as factors for additions, while resignations and retirements limited overall headcount growth • Japan's composite output index slipped to 52.1 from 52.3, its softest growth pace since May. Nov 5 : Australian data centre operator NEXTDC said on Thursday its board considered an aftermarket book build by an entity owned by Goodman Group and Digital Realty to be "opportunistic", and that it had received no takeover proposal. Shares of NEXTDC rallied in early trade, jumping as much as 45.8 per cent to A$9.52 by 2336 GMT and eyeing its strongest intraday gain ever. The stock had lost 45.8 per cent in October. On Wednesday, Goodman Group and Digital Realty offered to buy up to 9.9 per cent of NEXTDC in a deal worth about A$715 million ($501.14 million), Reuters reported, citing a term sheet. The share purchase comes after NEXTDC's stock plunged in October, when the company announced a power delay at its M3 Melbourne site, cut its guidance and shelved new development. The deal would give two rival data centre operators a stake of nearly 10 per cent in the Australian data centre operator.

FAST

SYDNEY, Nov 5 : An inquiry into data centres by Australia's most populous state found approvals failed to consider the cumulative effect on resources and infrastructure but stopped short of calling for a moratorium, prompting a blistering rebuke from its chair. The report by the New South Wales cross-party inquiry reflects a growing tension facing lawmakers globally as they navigate an AI-led buildout that McKinsey estimates will be worth $7 trillion by 2030: they want to benefit from the boom but communities are putting up increasingly robust resistance. The tension is especially strong in New South Wales, of which Sydney is the capital, where developer NextDC and ChatGPT owner OpenAI are awaiting approval for a data centre. There is a state election next March, and already residents in one suburb prompted a smaller project to be withdrawn. The report found the state lacked a coherent strategy to manage the data centre boom's impact on water, electricity and infrastructure. It warned current guidelines may underestimate future power demand and water supply limits, and that "clustering" facilities could create infrastructure pressures.

"The current planning framework assesses data centres primarily as individual developments despite many impacts being cumulative in nature," it said. "Data centre ... impacts are cumulative and are being felt across communities and other industries." But it stopped short of recommending a halt to approvals, and instead called for a comprehensive data centre strategy and better coordination between participants in the approvals pipeline. Minutes attached to the report showed members of the Public Accountability and Works Committee voted 6-1 to remove recommendations for a state and national moratorium on data centre approvals "until such time as all social and environmental harms can be fully understood". Committee chair Abigail Boyd, an upper house member from the Greens party who cast the lone vote to keep the recommendations, wrote in the report's foreword that an "AI-fuelled data centre frenzy" was "threatening to consume incomprehensibly large volumes of energy and water to feed their demands". "It is increasingly apparent that governments of all persuasions have been suckered in by an AI-fuelled get rich quick scheme, with data centres suiting the needs of governments short on ideas perfectly," she wrote. "But it's a false economy."

Source: Reuters

FAST

LONDON, Nov 5 : Climate change is becoming a growing threat to British sport, damaging facilities, disrupting fixtures, increasing costs and deterring participation, according to a report that warns the sector is dangerously under-prepared for extreme weather. Every organisation surveyed reported being affected by extreme weather in 2026 and 94 per cent said sport was under-prepared for climate change. Yet a separate review of professional club disclosures found only nine had explicitly identified climate or extreme weather as a business risk. The report by the British Association for Sustainable Sport (BASIS) paints a stark picture of a sporting landscape built for weather conditions that no longer exist, with impacts felt from Premier League stadiums to grassroots playing fields. "Sport is already paying the price for climate change through damaged grounds, rising insurance costs, lost match-day income and lost opportunities for people to be active," BASIS founder Russell Seymour said in the report.

"The game has changed. Extreme weather is no longer a series of isolated disruptions; it is a material, recurring and intensifying business risk." Among more than 200 clubs, venues and governing bodies surveyed, 86 per cent reported being affected by extreme heat, 78 per cent by drought, 31 per cent by storm damage and 28 per cent by flooding. The financial risks are becoming increasingly apparent. BASIS said 27 per cent of professional soccer, rugby league and rugby union stadiums it analysed in England face high direct flood risk, a figure projected to rise to 35 per cent under future climate scenarios. Several clubs have felt the impact. AFC Wimbledon reported nearly £900,000 ($1.2 million) in stadium flood costs in their 2025 accounts. MANCHESTER UNITED WARNING Manchester United have warned investors that extreme weather could damage property, disrupt match-day operations and cause losses that may not be fully covered by insurance. "If a club with Manchester United's scale and resources considers this risk sufficiently material to disclose to investors, smaller and less financially resilient institutions cannot reasonably treat it as peripheral," the report said. Worcestershire County Cricket Club's flood-prone New Road ground has repeatedly faced questions about its long-term viability, and Carlisle United have described flood insurance for Brunton Park as increasingly unaffordable. The report also highlighted the effect on competition schedules. Research cited by BASIS found at least 118 weather-related postponements across the top six tiers of English men's football between the 2021-22 and 2025-26 seasons, with lower-league and non-league clubs bearing the brunt. Cancelled or rearranged matches can mean lower attendances and reduced revenue for lower division clubs operating on tight budgets. The impact of Britain's long, hot and exceptionally dry summer became visible across sport in 2026. The Rugby Football Union (RFU) took the unprecedented step of postponing the start of the community rugby season in September because of rock-hard pitches and player welfare concerns. Beyond elite sport, BASIS warned that climate change risks undermining public health. Sport England found that nearly three-quarters of people affected by this year's unprecedented heatwaves participated in less sport and physical activity. The report called for climate resilience to become a boardroom priority across British sport, including dedicated adaptation plans, improved reporting and a £30 million annual fund to help protect grassroots facilities from increasingly volatile weather. ($1 = 0.7433 pounds)

NAPA, California, Nov 4 : The US federal government will lay out all the laws and regulations that apply to domestic AI labs later this month, Pentagon Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael said on Wednesday. Michael, who is vice chair of the government's Super Intelligence Task Force, said the group would publicize the regulatory landscape "in the next week or two." The task force is an intergovernmental agency established by President Donald Trump to establish AI policy. Michael, speaking at a Wall Street Journal technology conference in Napa, California, did not provide additional details. "What we're trying to do is create a framework that makes the American people have confidence that these companies are going to do the right thing," he said. "Or else I think what you get is 535 legislators writing a piece of regulation that could kill the industry."

Source: Reuters

FAST

LENS, France, Nov 4 : Como stormed into the Champions League record books with a stunning 9-1 demolition of Lens on Wednesday, equalling the biggest victory in the competition's history. The Italian side matched the eight-goal winning margins achieved by Liverpool and Real Madrid in 8-0 home victories over Besiktas and Malmo respectively. Como also became the first team since 1971 to score nine goals away from home in the European Cup and only the second after Bayern Munich to score nine in a Champions League match. Their third victory in four matches lifted them to fourth in the standings on nine points and continued a remarkable debut campaign in which they have scored 19 goals.

"It’s an incredible night," Como captain Lucas Da Cunha said. "We started with a lot of desire, we wanted to take the three points, like we always do, and this evening we were able to do that. "It's a crazy night and a crazy result, but we can't get ahead of ourselves." They led 3-0 at halftime, with Anastasios Douvikas scoring twice, before striking another five goals in a 22-minute spell after the break. Douvikas completed his hat-trick during that surge, while Ruben Aguilar pulled one back for Lens before Matteo Papaccioli rounded off the rout in stoppage time. Como's first Champions League campaign is already a resounding success, featuring dazzling 4–1 victories over both RB Leipzig and Manchester United. Their tally of 19 goals equals Queens Park Rangers' 1976 record for the most scored by a club in its first four matches in major European competition. Cesc Fabregas' side will next face AEK Athens and Real Betis before ending the league phase with more daunting tests against Paris St Germain and Barcelona. 'HUMILIATION' Lens, 33rd in the standings with three points, suffered the heaviest Champions League defeat by a French club. They also became the first team from Europe's top five leagues to concede nine goals at home in European competition. "The only word that comes to mind is a feeling of humiliation," Lens coach Yannick Cahuzac told Canal+. "We were dominated in every aspect of the game. It's hard to explain. "To concede a score like that, it goes beyond the game plan."

Source: Reuters

SAO PAULO, Nov 4 : Newly crowned Formula One world champion Kimi Antonelli paid tribute to his childhood hero Ayrton Senna on Wednesday, saying the late Brazilian's talent and dedication would continue to influence his approach to the sport after becoming the youngest driver to win the title. The 20-year-old Italian, who clinched the title with a third-place finish in Mexico on Sunday, spent time with members of Senna's family ahead of this weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix. He also sat in the cockpit of the Brazilian great's 1986 Lotus and visited his grave for the second year in a row. "Definitely the driver he was, he was incredible," Antonelli told Reuters on the sidelines of a Petronas event in Sao Paulo. "But as well, his work ethic, his attitude, how dedicated and how much passion he had for the sport. Then the person he was, very empathetic, someone who was trying to give back what he was receiving.

"All these things are the ones that caught my attention when I was a kid and that's why I got inspired by him from such a young age," he added about the Brazilian who died at Imola in 1994. Antonelli was frequently compared with Senna this season, with Mercedes boss Toto Wolff earlier this year cautioning against placing such expectations on the young Italian. Antonelli said he was still processing an emotional day with Senna's family as well as what happened on and off the track last weekend. VETTEL MESSAGE, MORE TO COME The significance of Antonelli's achievement was underlined by a video message from four-times world champion Sebastian Vettel, whose record as youngest champion was broken by the Italian. The 39-year-old German, who retired in 2022, urged Antonelli to enjoy the moment while reminding him that even if others now looked at him differently, success need not change the way he looked at them. "The message from Seb was very deep," Antonelli said.  "He says some things that are very true, that definitely my life will change a lot after this, but he also tells me to stay grounded because there's still, at the end of the day, a race to win. So that's a very important and very nice message from him." As Antonelli reflected on his breakthrough season, he also credited last year’s Sao Paulo Grand Prix with providing the momentum that eventually carried him to the 2026 title. His second-place finish at Interlagos in 2025, his then-best Formula One result, laid the foundations for his championship-winning year. "It was my most complete weekend of that year," he said. "I was coming from a very difficult period and the result definitely gave me the confidence that I needed to overcome that moment and try and move forward." With the championship secured, Antonelli said his ambitions remained unchanged. "We've done the first big step but there are many more to come," he said. "The goal is to try and win as much as possible, to be very successful for as long as possible... We're going to try to improve and come back even stronger."

Source: Reuters
